newsitem.title: USA: Wash. Mutual looks for Florida acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Wash. Mutual looks for Florida acquisitions.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc chief executive Kerry Killinger said he hopes to grow the company's presence in Florida internally and through acquisitions.

He spoke to reporters after a special shareholder meeting where Washington Mutual shareholders approved a merger with Great Western Financial Corp. Great Western shareholders also approved the deal on Friday.

"We have a very strong franchise (in Florida) with Great Western. We will look to add through that franchise with internal growth. And then we will also look for additional acquisitions to increase our presence there as well," he said.

The Great Western deal will add 120 Florida branches to the Washington Mutual franchise. Killinger said the thrift, which has completed 22 acquisitions in the last 10 years, is also interested in commercial bank acquisitions.
"We're interested in both thrift acquisitions and commercial bank acquisitions," he told reporters after the special shareholder meeting.

He said a commercial bank acquisition could be accomplished sooner than another thrift acquisition because Washington Mutual's commercial bank operations would not be involved with the Great Western integration.
"So if we found the right transaction on the commerical banking front that fit in well...certainly we would look at a timetable that would be much sooner than a major thrift aquisition," he said.
"That could potentially be at any time because those poeple are not burdened with operational integration," he said.
The principal areas would be in the northwest, with special focus on Washington, Oregon, Idaho, Utah and also California.
